excerpt: Second Front Systems (2F) runs Game Warden, a pre-accredited DevSecOps platform that helps software companies get DoD and FedRAMP authorization to sell to the US government.
content:
Second Front Systems, known as 2F, helps commercial software companies sell to the US government and its allies. Before software can run on government networks it needs an authority to operate (ATO) or FedRAMP authorisation, which traditionally takes a long time and a lot of compliance work. Second Front's answer is a pre-accredited platform: a vendor deploys its application on 2F's already-authorised environment and inherits much of the security paperwork, rather than building its own from scratch.

The main product is Game Warden, a DevSecOps platform. Second Front's product page says Game Warden is authorised for US Department of Defense deployment at Impact Levels 2 through 6 and on the top secret JWICS network, is certified at FedRAMP High, and can get applications through a DoD ATO or FedRAMP authorisation in as little as 90 days, including routes that do not need a government sponsor. It deploys to the customer's preferred cloud, with partnerships with AWS, Google Cloud and Microsoft. Other products include Frontier, for deploying and updating software on edge devices such as drones and vehicles in low-connectivity settings, and Workshop.

Customers cited by the company include Cohere, which in May 2026 said it achieved FedRAMP High authorisation through Game Warden in under 90 days by inheriting Second Front's controls. In January 2025 Second Front announced a partnership with Saab, Inc. to deploy and update edge systems such as the Enforcer 3.1 autonomous test vessel.

Second Front's about page says it was founded by former Marines frustrated by how slow government buying hurt front-line troops, and that it is a venture-backed public benefit company. Tyler Sweatt is CEO and chairman; the board includes Martha McSally as an independent director. The company also cites a place in Deloitte's 2024 Technology Fast 500 for North America.

Second Front does not publish prices. Its site says accreditation costs a fraction of the traditional route and asks vendors to get in touch.

This page is research, not a review. We have not used Game Warden; facts come from Second Front's pages and the press release listed under Sources.

profile.summary_short: Pre-accredited platform that gets commercial software DoD and FedRAMP authorised faster

use_cases: Getting a commercial SaaS product a DoD authority to operate
Reaching FedRAMP High authorisation by inheriting existing controls
Hosting software for classified and unclassified government networks

Entering UK and European defence markets

defence contractors deploying software to edge systems

buyers looking for a self-serve price list

pros: Authorised from IL2 to IL6 plus FedRAMP High
Can avoid the need for a government sponsor
Works across the major cloud providers
cons: Timelines and savings figures are the company's own claims

alternatives.intro: Other routes to government cloud authorisation for software vendors.

items.name: Palantir FedStart
items.what: Lets software companies run inside Palantir's accredited environment
items.difference: Backed by Palantir's own government authorisations.

items.name: AWS GovCloud (US)
items.what: Amazon's isolated cloud regions for US government workloads
items.difference: Infrastructure only; the vendor still has to earn its own authorisation.

items.name: Platform One (US Air Force)
items.difference: Run by the government itself rather than a vendor.

faq.a: Second Front's DevSecOps platform, authorised for DoD Impact Levels 2 to 6 and JWICS and certified at FedRAMP High, which vendors use to inherit compliance controls.

faq.q: How fast can Second Front get software authorised?
faq.a: The company claims a DoD ATO or FedRAMP authorisation in as little as 90 days. Cohere said it reached FedRAMP High in under 90 days through Game Warden.
Tyler Sweatt is CEO and chairman, according to the company's about page.
